name: Protecting Material Non-Public Information
title: Protecting Material Non-Public Information
answer: Protecting material non-public information in AI-related firms covers the handling of confidential data about models, training runs, partnerships, regulatory findings, and financial results before public disclosure. It applies to employees, contractors, board members, and automated systems that may access or generate such information. The scope includes both traditional corporate secrets and AI-specific outputs such as model weights, evaluation results, and deal terms involving data or compute. It also extends to information learned through AI tools that aggregate internal documents or communications.

sections.body: Protecting material non-public information in AI-related firms covers the handling of confidential data about models, training runs, partnerships, regulatory findings, and financial results before public disclosure. It applies to employees, contractors, board members, and automated systems that may access or generate such information. The scope includes both traditional corporate secrets and AI-specific outputs such as model weights, evaluation results, and deal terms involving data or compute. It also extends to information learned through AI tools that aggregate internal documents or communications.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The infrastructure for protecting MNPI typically includes access controls, data loss prevention systems, encrypted storage, and audit logging across internal platforms. In AI settings, this also covers model repositories, experiment tracking systems, and vector databases that may contain sensitive embeddings or fine-tuning data. Clean rooms and virtual data rooms are used for due diligence and partnership discussions. Monitoring tools flag unusual queries or bulk downloads from internal knowledge bases.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work is done through classification of information, need-to-know access policies, and pre-clearance procedures for trades and external communications. Teams map where MNPI resides, including in training data, model outputs, and meeting transcripts, then apply labels and automated redaction. Insider trading surveillance compares employee activity against a calendar of material events. Periodic training and attestations reinforce the distinction between public and non-public information.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Governance for MNPI protection sits with legal, compliance, and information security functions, often under a designated insider trading policy. It defines materiality thresholds, quiet periods, and reporting lines for potential breaches. Rights and risk include employee privacy limits on monitoring, contractual obligations to counterparties, and regulatory exposure if MNPI leaks or is misused. Provenance matters because AI-generated summaries can blur the origin of a fact, so systems record source documents and access history.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward automated classification and real-time monitoring of MNPI across unstructured data, including chat, code, and model outputs. Firms are testing ways to detect when a model has memorized confidential text or when an employee prompt reveals non-public context. Regulatory expectations are likely to tighten around AI tools that ingest internal data, pushing for explainable audit trails. The boundary between public model behavior and private training data will become a more explicit compliance concern.
